newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fedsure buys stake in Kingfisher Group.
newsitem.headline: Fedsure buys stake in Kingfisher Group.

text.p: South African financial services group Fedsure said on Tuesday that it had bought a 25.5 percent stake in Isle of Man-based Kingfisher Group in a move that marks the start of its overseas expansion.
Kingfisher specialises in international financial advice and the Fedsure buy is part of a joint-venture with NFB financial services group which has also bought a 25.5 percent stake.
"The deal marks the beginning of Fedsure's offshore expansion," Fedsure said in a statement.
Fedsure owns 49 percent of NFB and the remaining 49 percent of Kingfisher is owned by Hong Kong-based Top Corporate Network.
No price-tag for the stake was disclosed.
"Fedsure's acquisition forms part of our international strategy to provide clients with extended offshore financial services," said Bertrand Dedryver, Fedsure head of financial services and strategy.
Kingfisher aims its advice at corporates and high net-worth individuals.
Dedryver added the business should show growth potential, especially after South Africa relaxes some of its exchange controls.
On July 1, 35 years of foreign exchange controls will effectively be lifted when many ordinary South Africans get a green light to invest overseas for the first time.
